name: V8
summary: An embeddable JavaScript engine organized around isolate-owned heaps, context-specific execution environments, scoped handles, and garbage collection of unreachable heap objects.

features.name: Isolate and context execution boundary
features.description: V8 exposes an Isolate as a VM instance with its own heap and a Context as an execution environment for separate JavaScript applications within that isolate. Context creation is implemented through the embedding API and can use snapshots.
benefits: Separates heap ownership from JavaScript global environments
Allows multiple unrelated contexts to share one engine isolate
costs: Embedding code must manage isolate lifecycle and context entry
Context creation and global-object separation add state-management work

features.name: Scoped handles over a moving managed heap
features.description: V8's embedding guide describes handles as references to heap objects that remain valid when garbage collection moves objects. Local handles are grouped by HandleScope, while persistent handles can outlive a function scope.
benefits: Provides a stable embedding reference model despite object relocation
Allows short-lived and long-lived references to use different lifetime controls
costs: Embedders must obey handle-scope lifetime rules
Persistent handles require explicit lifecycle management

features.name: Reachability-based garbage collection
features.description: V8's embedding documentation states that the collector reclaims heap objects inaccessible from JavaScript and without handles, and that collection may move objects while updating handles. The fixed source exposes heap-level collector selection and collection stages.
benefits: Supports compaction and relocation while preserving handle references
costs: Collection and relocation impose runtime coordination costs
Native embedders must maintain correct handle references

mathematical_views.question: How do isolate, context, and handle-scope transitions constrain embedded JavaScript execution?
assumptions: Isolates own heap state and contexts own execution-global state
Handle scopes define nested reference-lifetime regions
The view abstracts scheduling, compiler tiers, and embedder-specific callbacks

mathematical_views.question: How can garbage collection reclaim or relocate heap objects while preserving the validity of embedder references?
assumptions: Heap objects form a reachability graph from JavaScript roots and handles
Unreachable objects are eligible for collection
The collector updates managed handles when objects move, while native raw pointers are outside this abstraction

benefits: Reusable engine heap with separate execution environments
costs: Embedder lifecycle and entry rules add complexity
Collection introduces coordination and latency costs
